name: api-versioning-without-breaking-clients-p1
prompt: how do I evolve our public API without breaking the apps already calling the old endpoints

chunks.content: the docs site got a two-column layout so navigation stays visible while scrolling
added a partial index on active subscriptions to speed the renewal sweep
the migration tool stamps a schema version row so it knows which up-scripts still need to run against the database
hard email bounces now mark the address undeliverable so we stop retrying them
we force users on app builds older than six months to update before they can log in, since those old clients miss critical security fixes
per-key rate limits return a Retry-After header when a caller is throttled
the search box debounces input and shows typeahead suggestions after two characters
large CSV exports stream chunked so the browser starts downloading immediately
third-party tokens refresh silently in the background before they expire
the redesigned billing page is behind a flag for internal users only
within a version we only make additive changes: new optional fields and new endpoints are fine, but we never remove a field or change its meaning so existing callers keep working untouched
clients pin a version through the URL prefix or an Accept header, and an unspecified request defaults to the oldest supported contract so old integrations are never silently upgraded
a retiring version keeps running for a published sunset window while we emit a Deprecation header and email the affected API keys, giving old apps time to migrate before anything is removed
each API call logs its version and key so we can see who is still on the old contract
